question:
A 65-year-old Caucasian man visits the nephrology outpatient clinic for a follow-up appointment. He was previously diagnosed with stage G3a chronic kidney disease (CKD) and albuminuria stage A2. He follows strict dietary recommendations and takes enalapril. He has a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia which has been complicated by urinary tract obstruction. His vitals are stable, and his blood pressure is within the recommended limits. His most recent laboratory studies are as follows:
Serum sodium 140 mEq/L
Serum potassium 5.8 mEq/L
Serum chloride 102 mEq/L
Serum phosphate 4.0 mg/dL
Hemoglobin 11.5 mg/dL
Albumin excretion rate (AER) 280 mg/day
Which of the following is the best strategy in the management of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Stage G3a CKD and albuminuria A2" -> "Increased risk of hyperkalemia due to impaired kidney function" -> "High serum potassium levels (5.8 mEq/L)" -> "Potential need for potassium-lowering therapy" -> 80% CHAIN: "Enalapril" -> "ACE inhibitor" -> "May contribute to hyperkalemia by reducing aldosterone secretion" -> "Possible exacerbation of high serum potassium levels" -> 70% CHAIN: "Addition of furosemide" -> "Loop diuretic" -> "Promotes potassium excretion" -> "May help lower serum potassium levels" -> 75% CHAIN: "Observation" -> "Continued monitoring of serum potassium levels" -> "May not actively address the hyperkalemia issue" -> 60% CHAIN: "Addition of patiromer" -> "Potassium binder" -> "Binds to potassium in the gut, reducing absorption" -> "Potential for lowering serum potassium levels" -> 85% CHAIN: "Addition of sevelamer" -> "Phosphate binder" -> "May not directly impact serum potassium levels" -> "Unlikely to address the hyperkalemia concern" -> 80%
analysis: The patient has stage G3a CKD with albuminuria and hyperkalemia. Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor that can cause hyperkalemia. The best strategy would be to remove enalapril and consider alternative medications.
